reader_summary.headline: Host analyzes Limbach's missed data center boom and potential recovery after a stock drop.
reader_summary.overview: Limbach stock fell after revenue dropped, but the host believes the business is fixed. The company missed the data center growth by focusing only on owner direct work. A recent acquisition is the first real move to fix this lack of exposure.

key_points.text: Limbach stock dropped 50% after revenue fell, but the host believes the business is fixed and missed the data center growth.
key_points.evidence_quote: Limbach spent three years turning itself from a general contractor into an owner direct services business, and the market loved it right up until this summer. Then organic revenue went down mid single digits, EBITDA fell 30%, guidance came down from $90m to $80m, and the stock lost half its value.

key_points.text: The host argues the company missed the data center boom because it focused only on owner direct work while competitors grew.
key_points.evidence_quote: While FIX and EME compounded on data centers, Limbach stayed singularly focused on owner direct work and ended up with effectively zero data center exposure.

key_points.text: A recent acquisition is the first real move to fix the company's lack of data center exposure.
key_points.evidence_quote: The CYMCOR acquisition announced alongside Q2 is the first real move to fix that.

thesis: The episode argues that Limbach (LMB) is a compelling buy because the market has unfairly punished it for missing the data center boom, while the company is now positioning to fix this exposure via acquisition. The speaker contends that the EBITDA decline reflects fixed cost deleverage on a temporary demand pocket rather than a broken business, and that the stock is undervalued relative to peers like FIX and EME which successfully compounded on data centers.

claims.claim: Celsius is undervalued compared to competitors like Monster and Coke, and the market is ignoring the value of the Alani Nu acquisition.
claims.quote: Celsius trades at ~20x earnings while growing ~18% a year, cheaper than Monster (~34x) and even Coke (~25x) despite faster growth. The Pershing Square Challenge third-place team makes the long case for $CELH: the market is sleeping on the Alani Nu acquisition

claims.claim: The market has not fully appreciated Baker Hughes' evolution from a cyclical oil field services business to one with a long runway for its IET business.
claims.quote: Team Baker Hughes, the second-place finishers in the 2026 Pershing Square Challenge, discuss their Baker Hughes thesis and why they believe the market hasn't fully appreciated the company's evolution from a cyclical oil field services business.

claims.claim: DoorDash's growth story still has room to run, with new verticals and international expansion potentially leading to earlier profitability.
claims.quote: The winners of the Pershing Square Challenge 2026 discuss their Doordash pitch, including why the growth story still has room to run (and the 90 primary research calls they made to back up that call).

claims.claim: Pershing Square US is expected to trade at a premium to its net asset value rather than a discount, and the fund deserves a premium multiple to peers.
claims.quote: James Elbaor of Marlton makes the case that $PSUS will trade at a premium to NAV instead of the typical closed-end fund discount and that $PS will ultimately trade at a premium multiple to peers like Blackstone, KKR, Apollo and Carlyle

claims.claim: Take 5 remains a crown jewel that could be worth the entire enterprise value of the company, making other businesses a free option.
claims.quote: Kyle Mowery (GrizzlyRock Capital) walks through why Take 5 remains a crown jewel and could be worth the entire EV of the company (making the franchise and autoglass businesses a free option).

claims.claim: Liberty Global is cheap on a sum-of-the-parts basis and an upcoming Ziggo spin is expected to crystallize value.
claims.quote: Rich Howe of Stock Spin-Off Investing makes the bull case for Liberty Global ($LBTYK): cheap on a sum-of-the-parts, an upcoming Ziggo spin to crystallize value, and a hidden ventures portfolio.

claims.claim: The speaker believes the EBITDA decline is due to fixed cost deleverage on a demand air pocket rather than a broken business, and that the company missed the data center boom which is the bigger story.
claims.quote: His argument is that the EBITDA decline is fixed cost deleverage on a demand air pocket, not a broken business, and that the bigger story is the one Limbach missed.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that while other companies compounded on data centers, Limbach focused on owner direct work and now has a move to fix its data center exposure via an acquisition.
claims.quote: While FIX and EME compounded on data centers, Limbach stayed singularly focused on owner direct work and ended up with effectively zero data center exposure. The CYMCOR acquisition announced alongside Q2 is the first real move to fix that.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that the host Yaron Naymark is back buying Limbach after a significant drawdown, indicating a strong buy view.
claims.quote: Yaron Naymark of 1 Main Capital pitched me this name in June 2023, watched it 6.5x, sold most of it, and is back buying it after a 75% drawdown.
